inline_comments.comment: This narrows the match condition from the original `[it.componentName, it.localImportName, it.importName].includes(componentName)` to only `it.componentName === componentName`, silently breaking cases where `meta.component` references the package-export name while the story uses a local alias. For example: `import { Button as Btn } from '@ds/ui'; export default { component: Button }` — here `csf._meta?.component` resolves to `'Button'` (the identifier used in the source), `componentName` (the JSX element name) is `'Btn'`, and `importName` is `'Button'`. The original code matched on `importName`; the new code does not. Consider restoring the multi-field check: `[it.componentName, it.localImportName, it.importName].some(v => v === componentName)`.

`fs.watch(dir, { recursive: true }, ...)` is not supported on Linux in Node.js versions prior to 22.0.0 (added in Node.js 22 via inotify). On Linux systems running Node 18 or 20 (common in CI and production), this throws `ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM`. The `catch` block silently swallows the error and logs only at `debug` level, so file-watching silently never starts — props will not refresh after file edits during dev mode on the most common server/CI platform. Consider using a cross-platform watching library such as `chokidar` (already present in the repo) that handles Linux recursive watching via inotify and emits consistent events, or at minimum emit a `logger.warn` when the recursive watcher fails to indicate that watch mode is degraded.

`watch` is typed as `boolean` (required) in the preset options type, but `getManifests` in `manifests.ts` is declared as `{ watch?: boolean }` and is called without `watch` from `writeManifests`, which passes `undefined` at runtime. TypeScript's type-checking is silently bypassed by the `PresetPropertyFn` generic. Change to `watch?: boolean` to correctly reflect optionality, matching the actual call sites and preventing confusion for future preset implementers.

`this.commandLine.fileNames.includes(fileName)` is O(n) inside a loop over `fileNames`, making `ensureFiles` O(n²). For a project like Mantine (9 tsconfig projects, each with hundreds of files) this may be called with dozens of story/component paths per manifest request. Pre-convert the file list to a `Set<string>` before the loop — `const existing = new Set(this.commandLine.fileNames)` — and use `existing.has(fileName)` for O(1) lookup.

`this.entries = entries` replaces the stored entry set on every call to `extractPropsFromStories`. The warmup timer (fired after file changes) re-runs only the last assigned `entries`. If two callers use the same `ComponentMetaProject` with different entry sets — for example, the component debugger preview and the live manifest serve path — the warmup will only replay the most-recent caller's entries, silently leaving the earlier caller's types stale after a file change. Consider accumulating entries with deduplication (e.g. a `Map<storyFilePath+exportName, StoryExtractionEntry>`) rather than wholesale replacement.

`arrayItemsEqual` treats arrays as unordered sets: it builds `new Set(a)` and checks each element of `b`. This means `['x', 'x', 'y']` and `['x', 'y', 'y']` are considered equal — same length (3), same distinct elements. TypeScript file lists don't contain duplicates in practice so this is currently safe, but it should either be named `setItemsEqual` or use a correct array equality approach (e.g. sort both and compare element-by-element) to match its stated contract.

`this.getProjectForFile(absoluteImportPath)` uses the **story** file path to select the tsconfig project. In monorepos where stories live in `apps/storybook/` (with their own tsconfig) and components in `packages/ui/` (with a separate tsconfig that is *not* referenced by the stories tsconfig), `program.getSourceFile(entry.componentPath)` inside `extractPropsFromStories` will return `undefined` and the entry will be silently dropped. Consider using `component.path` (the component file) as the primary project-selection key, or at least attempt both the story and component paths when the first resolves no matching source file.

`resolvePropsFromStoryFile` only handles named imports (`isNamedImports`) and default imports. Namespace imports (`import * as Accordion from './accordion'`) are not handled — the `importSymbol` is never assigned for `isNamespaceImport` bindings, so `<Accordion.Root />` in a story using a namespace import silently falls through to Path 2 (requires explicit `meta.component`). This is a real pattern in story files that pair with compound-component design systems. Consider adding a `typescript.isNamespaceImport(clause.namedBindings)` branch that assigns `importSymbol = checker.getSymbolAtLocation(clause.namedBindings.name)`.

Five tests are removed with the comment "RDT returns [] for all of these". If these patterns genuinely regressed in the react-docgen-typescript engine as a side-effect of this PR, the tests should be updated to assert `[]` rather than deleted — that documents the known limitation and guards against accidental re-breakage. If they regressed before this PR, the comment should cite the PR or issue that introduced the regression. Deleting passing tests without replacement permanently removes the spec for RDT behavior on `ForwardRef`, `RenamedExport`, `DisplayNameOverride`, and `Barrel` patterns.

`--max_old_space_size` is bumped from 4096 to 5120 with no explanation. If this is needed because the persistent `ComponentMetaManager` LanguageService retains additional TypeScript program state in memory during the UI Storybook build, add an inline comment stating why (e.g. `# Increased from 4096: persistent TS LanguageService for react-component-meta retains additional heap`). Without context, future maintainers cannot judge whether to revert or raise this limit further.

general_comments.comment: The PR description is excellent and the new files are well-commented with Volar-pattern attribution. However, `resolvePropsFromStoryFile` in `componentMetaExtractor.ts` has a known silent fallback for three important cases — namespace imports, package imports that fail to resolve, and stories with no JSX — each of which falls through to Path 2 (meta.component required). None of these fallthrough paths log even a debug message. For users debugging why props aren't appearing for a component, a `logger.debug('[reactComponentMeta] Path 1 skipped for <reason>: falling back to Path 2')` trace per entry would significantly reduce support cost.

The `ComponentMetaManager` singleton (`getInstance()`) registers a `process.on('exit', ...)` handler each time it is first constructed but never deregisters it. More importantly, `ComponentMetaManager.instance` (the static Promise) is never reset after `dispose()` is called. In test environments that call `dispose()` on an instance obtained via `getInstance()`, subsequent calls to `getInstance()` return the already-disposed manager rather than creating a fresh one. The test files in this PR sidestep the issue by constructing `new ComponentMetaManager(ts)` directly, but any test that exercises the singleton path (e.g. a future integration test for `generator.ts`) would silently operate on a disposed manager. Add a static `reset()` method or null out `ComponentMetaManager.instance` inside `dispose()`.
